name: Norte de Santander
summary_text: This frontier department is covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no department-specific legal, enforcement or incident finding beyond the national and departmental homicide counts: no deviation from the national position is material enough to score separately (±0.02), so it is assessed at the national score. Context that does apply here: Norte de Santander sits in the country's frontier/border belt where 'orden público' regimes mean armed groups rather than departmental police effectively regulate conduct, and Caribe Afirmativo's 2025 report documents the territorial expansion of violence and insufficiency of state response, with trans women displaced from such departments because of their gender identity by the same armed actors that displace others.

sources.title: The transphobic murder that has shocked Colombia | International | EL PAÍS English
sources.claim_summary: El País in English (14 Apr 2025) on the killing of Sara Millerey (32), a trans woman, in Bello, Antioquia: beaten and thrown into a creek, died of her injuries, onlookers filmed instead of helping; the third LGBTQ+ killing in Bello in 2025; 13 trans people killed nationally in Q1 2025. National context — no Norte de Santander-specific content.

sources.title: Sara Millerey’s brutal murder shocked Colombia. The killings didn’t stop there | CNN
sources.claim_summary: CNN (6 Aug 2025) follow-up in the 'As Equals' series: the viral Millerey video shocked the country but the killings continued — armed gangs; frames being queer in parts of the country as 'to sign your own death sentence'. National context.

sources.title: ‘We are killed for what we are’: trans women in Colombia targeted by armed groups | Global development | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: The Guardian (30 Jul 2024): armed groups threatening a wave of 'social cleansing' against trans women in Caquetá — Tatiana Cespedes (51) given a week to leave or be killed, twice displaced; 41 trans women killed in the country in 2023, 8 killed Feb–Apr 2024; flyers circulating by WhatsApp list trans women as legitimate military targets. Documents the armed-group threat model that also applies to frontier departments including Norte de Santander.
